To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the DNA damage repair protein PARP-1 is associated with DNA in cells undergoing repair after exposure to the alkylating agent MMS, and that the association is increased in cells that have been treated with a PARP inhibitor and MMS, as compared with cells that have been exposed only to MMS.
PARP inhibition results in increased association of PARP- with DNA in cells undergoing DNA repair, and this likely contributes to the extreme hypersensitivity of these cells to alkylation damage.
PARP inhibition in cells with DNA alkylation damage causes PARP-1 association with DNA and that this association increases with time after treatment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanism of action of the small molecule inhibitor of the DNA repair protein PARP-1.
understanding the mechanism of the extreme hypersensitivity of base excision-repair proficient mouse cells treated with methylmethanesulfonate and the PARP inhibitor ABT-888.
the role of PARP in the repair of alkyation damage in mammalian cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of PARP inhibitors with alkylating agents is highly effective for killing cancer cells, but that the mechanism of action of this combination therapy remains to be fully defined.
the combination of MMS and a potent PARP-1 inhibitor causes a dramatic increase in PARP-1 binding to chromatin in the cells, which is a likely mechanism for the hypersensitivity phenotype.
inhibition of PARP-2 activity in cells with DNA damage results in the formation of PARP-3 complexes that are not able to repair the damage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found that PARP inhibitors are effective in killing cells that are deficient in base excision repair, and that this effect is due to inhibition of PARP-2 and PARP-3.
PARP inhibition in the presence of alkylation damage causes a striking cell killing phenomenon that requires DNA repair, DNA replication, and PARP-1 expression.

PARP inhibitors are effective against tumors that are dependent on PARP activity for survival, but that they are also effective against tumors that do not have an elevated PARP activity, such as tumors that are defective in the DNA double strand break repair system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PARP-1 is associated with DNA repair intermediates in alkylation damage–induced cells.
PARP inhibition in cells with DNA damage can result in PARP-1 becoming associated with DNA repair intermediates and blocking repair and replication.
PARP inhibition can be a very effective treatment strategy, but it must be combined with a chemotherapeutic drug that damages DNA.
